parsed.claim: For every d, the set of quotients f(0)/𝓕f(0) over FullAdmissible d is bounded below (by 0). Hence sInf in fullLinearProgram is not the junk value caused by being unbounded below. This uses Fourier inversion: f(0) = ∫ 𝓕f ≥ 0.
parsed.lean:
theorem probe_bdd_below (d : ℕ) : BddBelow (PackingBounds.fullQuotientSet d) := by
  refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
  rintro _ ⟨f, rfl⟩
  unfold PackingBounds.fullQuotient
  refine div_nonneg ?_ f.fourier_zero_pos.le
  have h1 : (𝓕⁻ (𝓕 f.function) : CohnElkies.TestFunction d) = f.function := by
    first
      | exact FourierTransform.fourierInv_fourier_eq _
      | exact SchwartzMap.fourierInv_fourier_eq _
      | simp
  have h3 : ((𝓕⁻ (𝓕 f.function) : CohnElkies.TestFunction d) : CohnElkies.Euclidean d → ℂ) 0
      = ∫ v, (𝓕 f.function) v := by
    first
      | (rw [SchwartzMap.fourierInv_coe, Real.fourierInv_eq']; simp)
      | (simp [SchwartzMap.fourierInv_coe, Real.fourierInv_eq'])
  have hinv : f.function 0 = ∫ v, (𝓕 f.function) v := by
    calc f.function 0 = ((𝓕⁻ (𝓕 f.function) : CohnElkies.TestFunction d) : CohnElkies.Euclidean d → ℂ) 0 := by rw [h1]
      _ = _ := h3
  have h4 : (∫ v, (𝓕 f.function) v).re = ∫ v, ((𝓕 f.function) v).re := by
    first
      | exact (integral_re (SchwartzMap.integrable (𝓕 f.function))).symm
      | simpa using (integral_re (SchwartzMap.integrable (𝓕 f.function))).symm
  rw [hinv, h4]
  exact integral_nonneg (fun v => f.fourier_nonneg v)
